source.quote:
[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by statute on June 14, 1935. The sole operative command approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act ('do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry.'); the introductory recital and the five numbered findings command nothing. Actor: Congress, S.J. Res. 113, section 2, approved June 14, 1935. Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935; EO 6900 and EO 7020 amend the code and are later events, not ends.

original_representation.quote:
Whereas, the Secretary of Agriculture having submitted for my approval a Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry and having rendered his report and recommendations and findings thereon:

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby find that:

1. An application has been duly made, pursuant to and in full compliance with the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, for my approval of a Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry; and,

2. Due notice and opportunity for hearings to interested parties have been given pursuant to the provisions of the Act and regulations thereunder; and,

3. Hearings have been held upon said Code, pursuant to such notice and pursuant to the pertinent provisions of the Act and regulations thereunder; and,

4. Said Code of Fair Competition constitutes a Code of Fair Competition, as contemplated by the Act and complies in all respects with the pertinent provisions of the Act, including clauses (1) and (2) of subsection (a) of Section 3 of Title I of the Act; and,

5. It appears, after due consideration, that said Code of Fair Competition will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress as declared in Section 1 of Title I of the Act.

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

December 27, 1933.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 6847-A—Terminating Stay of the Provisions of Section 1 of Article IX of Code of Fair Competition for the Wheat Flour Milling Industry; September 14, 1934; APP node 373333; common-crawl capture 2024-10-12T15:08:08Z
source.quote:
Whereas, a Code of Fair Competition for the Wheat Flour Milling Industry was approved by me June 9, 1934; and

Whereas, the Executive Order approving such Code stayed the provisions of Article IX thereof until such time as the Secretary of Agriculture determines and declares in writing, after adequate investigation, that an emergency exists in the wheat flour milling industry, and then only for such periods of time and to the extent that the provisions of such article are found by the Secretary to be necessary to meet the circumstances of such emergency; and

Whereas, it appears from facts presented by members of the industry that such stay should be modified in order to effectuate the declared policy of the National Industrial Recovery Act:

Now, therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby order that the stay of the provisions of Section 1 of Article IX of such Code be terminated. Except as provided herein, the provisions of the Executive Order of June 9, 1934, approving such Code, shall remain in full force and effect.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 14, 1934.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated on 1934-09-14, the date the order issued: the clause only terminates a stay ('do hereby order that the stay of the provisions of Section 1 of Article IX of such Code be terminated'), a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards and is exhausted by performance on its own date. Actor: EO 6847-A itself; the cited text is the order's own operative sentence. The code provision that the termination released, Section 1 of Article IX, operated only through the code, whose approval and enforcement ended with the repeal on 1935-06-14 under section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 ('All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed'); that repeal is recorded as a later event of the code, not as the end of this exhausted clause, and the surviving consequence is not a continuing command of this order. Schechter (1935-05-27) is a validity characterization of the section 3 delegation, not an end date for this order.

[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

source.quote:
The Administrator for Industrial Recovery having called a public hearing to determine whether my order approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade, Dated December 30, 1933, should be canceled, and the hearing having been held and tho National Industrial Recovery Board having rendered its report containing its recommendations and findings with respect to such cancellation, and it appearing that upon such cancellation most of the transportation operations of this Trade will be subject to the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry approved February 10, 1934, and all of the construction operations thereof to the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry approved January 31, 1934.

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States pursuant to the authority vested in me by Article VIII of the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade, and by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (approved June 16, 1933) do adopt and approve the report, recommendations and findings of the National Industrial Recovery Board, and do hereby cancel my order approving said Code.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

Approval recommended:

     National Industrial Recovery Board

By W. A. HARRIMAN

          Administrative Officer

The White House,

December 19, 1934.

Actor: EO 6925-A itself; the cited text is the order's own operative sentence. The surviving consequence, that the order approving the Code of Fair Competition for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade stands cancelled, is separate from the exhausted command and is not a continuing command of this order. The order is not a code approval and the repeal of June 14, 1935 (section 2 of S.J. Res. 113) is not its end; the approval it cancelled had already ended on 1934-12-19. Schechter (1935-05-27) is a validity characterization of the section 3 delegation, not an end date for this order.

Whereas the Federal Alcohol Control Administration has submitted for my approval amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry and has rendered its report and recommendations and findings thereon; and

Whereas due notice of public hearing on said proposed amendments has been given and a public hearing thereon has been held pursuant to such notice;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act of June 16, 1933 (ch. 90, 48 Stat. 195), and in order to effectuate the purposes of said Title, I hereby approve said amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

April 19, 1935.

research_rationale:
EO 7020 (April 19, 1935, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act and modifies the President's previous approval of the code 'to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended.' The held text has two 'Whereas' recitals (the Federal Alcohol Control Administration's submission, report and findings; notice and public hearing) and one operative sentence beginning 'Now, Therefore'. The machine inventory is one clause spanning the whole text including the recitals and the signature line; I replaced it with one clause, characters 370 to 778, the operative sentence (inventory correction recorded). Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-7020-amending-code-fair-competition-for-the-wine-industry.txt, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; 837 characters). APP page check (AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, working-text paragraph): the jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with sha256 1c4e2fc939d17af99a84d4e21389c7c9826eb6eb92a4e46e8ad2cca7ad05f747 is headed 'Executive Order 7020—Amending Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry', dated April 19, 1935, node app:node/376488, Common Crawl capture 2025-09-05T13:49:16Z; its text_sha256 26466d12d15896a87d7171ff47b2fc3362c292446035ebac28549c83c06dbd79 equals the sha256 I computed for the held file, and the page heading (which names the number), the date and the subject agree with the text. Cotton holds the exact page bytes (jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output/captures). Identity also agrees with the census register row and the WPA 1944 list (page 610: 'Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry approved.'). Legal basis for the first end. An approval of a code under section 3 of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act had legal effect only through section 3: under 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry and a violation in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce was an unfair method of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and district attorneys were directed to sue, and under 3(f) each violation was a misdemeanor (the section 3 excerpt held in this packet). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935 (49 Stat. 375), repealed 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes' and states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the power the approval rested on and every provision through which the approved code was enforced, which is the reason (not a default date) that it ends the prospective operative effect of this command on June 14, 1935. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495 (decided May 27, 1935), held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional ('we hold the code provisions here in question to be invalid'); the held excerpts record that as a validity characterization (an approval under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing, and May 27, 1935 is when that was declared), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no other approving order and a later doctrine treats a measure's earlier existence as an operative fact. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced the two-year expiry in section 2(c) with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2.

source.quote:
[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date.
source_notes.reason: Schechter judgment: the code provisions in question held invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground; recorded as a validity characterization of approvals under section 3, not as an end of this order.
